name: FDA and EMA Good AI Practice Principles
blurb: The ten principles the FDA and EMA agreed for AI across the medicine lifecycle.
title: FDA and EMA Good AI Practice Principles
answer: In January 2026 the FDA and EMA published ten shared principles for good AI practice in drug development, covering research, manufacturing and pharmacovigilance. They are high level: human centred design, a risk based approach, data quality, clear documentation, lifecycle monitoring and clear, essential information for users. They signal that both agencies will judge AI by the same basic tests.

reading.body:
In January 2026 the FDA and EMA agreed ten shared principles for good AI practice across the medicine lifecycle, meaning both agencies will judge AI by the same basic tests.

The principles span research, manufacturing and pharmacovigilance, and they are deliberately high level: human centred design, a risk based approach, data quality, clear documentation, lifecycle monitoring, and clear essential information for users. The pattern is convergence rather than novelty. Two regulators with different legal systems settled on one vocabulary for what good practice looks like, and that vocabulary is procedural rather than technical. None of the ten turns on model architecture, training compute, or where the model runs.

For AI specifically, the practical consequence is that a governance policy can be written once and mapped to both agencies. The listed tests are about documentation, monitoring and user information, which are the parts of an AI system that survive model updates and vendor changes. A team that treats the ten principles as a checklist is building the evidence trail regulators will ask for, not a technical standard.

What the data does not cover is enforcement. It records that the principles were issued and what they contain, not how either agency will apply them, what evidence will satisfy them, or whether they carry the force of guidance or regulation. It also says nothing about compute, data centres or power, and nothing in the ten principles as described reaches that layer.

sections.body: Use the ten principles as the checklist for an AI governance policy. A policy that maps to them will read well to both agencies.
